notes.text: **Zohar II 88b (Yitro)** — "אַתְקִינוּ סְעוּדָתָא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא עִלָּאָה, אַתְקִינוּ סְעוּדָתָא דְּמַלְכָּא". When Rabbi Shimon came to his Shabbat meal he would announce: prepare the meal of supernal faith, prepare the meal of the King. Rav Tzadok takes the Zohar's two titles for the Shabbat meal as two separate kinds of holy eating, which the rest of the os sets out. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar III 230a (Pinchas, Ra'aya Mehemna)** — "אִיהוּ אֱמֶת, וְאִיהִי אֱמוּנָה". In the Zohar's list of paired names, the Holy One is Truth and His Shechinah is Faith. So "faith" (מהימנותא) points to Malchut, the Shechinah, which the Name Adonai represents. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 64a** (the last lines of the tractate) — "כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדָה שֶׁתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹכָהּ, כְּאִילּוּ נֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו שְׁכִינָה". Whoever enjoys a meal where a Torah scholar is present is as though he enjoyed the radiance of the Shechinah. The Gemara asks: did they eat before God? They ate before Moshe! Rav Tzadok answers that "Elohim" here is the Shechinah. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Shabbat 64a)*

**Exodus 18:12** — "וַיָּבֹא אַהֲרֹן וְכֹל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֶאֱכׇל לֶחֶם עִם חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים". Aharon and the elders came to eat bread with Moshe's father-in-law before God. This is the verse Berakhot 64a reads (quoted as given there). *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 31b (Bereishis)** — "אֱלֹהִים עִלָּאָה. אֱלֹהִים דְּפַחַד יִצְחָק. אֱלֹהִים בַּתְרָאָה". On "אשר לו אלהים קרובים" (Deuteronomy 4:7), R. Yosei says there are three Elohim: the supernal one, the Elohim of the Fear of Yitzchak, and the last Elohim. The last Elohim is the Shechinah (Malchut), the Elohim of the Creation account. The Mafteach gives Zohar I 31a. The tools could not settle whether this paragraph stands on 31a or 31b. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar II 22b (Va'era)** — "מֹשֶׁה, אִלְמָלֵא דְּהֲוָה מָארֵיהּ דְּבֵיתָא, אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים, אִתְעַנָּשׁ עַל מַה דְּאָמַר". Had Moshe not been the master of the house, "the man of God" (Deuteronomy 33:1), he would have been punished for what he said. Rav Tzadok draws on the Zohar's reading of "איש האלהים" as husband of the Shechinah: eating before Moshe is eating before Elohim. *Mafteach: found*

**Avot 3:3** — "שְׁלשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד וְאָמְרוּ עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּאִלּוּ אָכְלוּ מִשֻּׁלְחָנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם". When three eat at one table and speak words of Torah there, it is as though they ate from the table of the Omnipresent. This gives him the phrase "שֻׁלְחָנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם" in [1.15]. *Mafteach: found*

**Ezekiel 41:22** — "הַמִּזְבֵּחַ עֵץ ... וַיְדַבֵּר אֵלַי זֶה הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי ה'". In the prophet's verse the altar is called "the table before Hashem". That is why Rav Tzadok takes a table with Torah at it to be an altar, eaten in the Name Havayah. The Mafteach indexes Avot 3:3 but not the verse. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ketubot 104a** — "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁיָּגַעְתִּי בְּעֶשֶׂר אֶצְבְּעוֹתַי בַּתּוֹרָה, וְלֹא נֶהֱנֵיתִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה". As he was dying, Rebbi raised his ten fingers: I toiled in Torah with all ten, and did not benefit from this world even with my little finger. *Mafteach: found*

**Avodah Zarah 11a** — "זֶה אַנְטוֹנִינוּס וְרַבִּי, שֶׁלֹּא פָּסְקוּ מֵעַל שׁוּלְחָנָם לֹא חֲזֶרֶת וְלֹא קִישּׁוּת וְלֹא צְנוֹן, לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים". Lettuce, cucumber and radish never left the tables of Antoninus and Rebbi, summer or winter. The same statement appears in Berakhot 57b. Together the two sources show the tzaddik's level: a full royal table, yet no bodily pleasure at all. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar II 61b (Beshalach)** — "מְזוֹנָא עִלָּאָה יַתִּיר מִכֹּלָּא, הוּא מְזוֹנָא דְּחַבְרַיָּיא, אִינּוּן דְּמִשְׁתַּדְּלֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, דְּאַכְלֵי מְזוֹנָא דְּרוּחָא וְנִשְׁמְתָא ... וְאִקְרֵי חָכְמָה". The highest food is the food of the companions who toil in Torah. They eat food of spirit and soul, drawn from the supernal place called Wisdom. Hence his "level of the sage" (מדרגת חכם). *Mafteach: found*

**Ecclesiastes 7:12** — "וְיִתְרוֹן דַּעַת הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ". Wisdom gives life to those who have it. The Zohar (II 61b–62a) quotes this verse to close its passage on the companions' food. *Mafteach: found*

**Deuteronomy 8:3** (unnamed) — "כִּי עַל כׇּל מוֹצָא פִי ה' יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם". Man lives by all that comes out of Hashem's mouth. The sage eats the divine word that keeps the food in being, not only its body. *Mafteach: missing*

**Proverbs 9:5** — "לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי". Wisdom calls: come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed. Torah itself is the bread the sage eats. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 10b** — "כָּל הַמְאָרֵחַ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וּמְהַנֵּהוּ מִנְּכָסָיו — מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ מַקְרִיב תְּמִידִין". One who hosts a Torah scholar and lets him benefit from his property is credited as though he offered the daily offerings. The Gemara learns this from the Shunammite and Elisha. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 4** (Rav Tzadok) — uses Yoma 71a and Berakhot 10b to read Malki-Tzedek's "לחם ויין" to Avraham, the first Torah scholar, as meal-offerings and libations. Bread for a scholar is a mincha, wine a nesech, and so "והוא כהן לאל עליון". *checked*

**Yoma 71a** — "הָרוֹצֶה לְנַסֵּךְ יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ — יְמַלֵּא גְּרוֹנָם שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן". Whoever wishes to pour wine on the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine. R. Berachyah learns it from "אֲלֵיכֶם אִישִׁים אֶקְרָא" (Proverbs 8:4). Rav Tzadok uses it again in [2.34] for Yaakov's wine. *Mafteach: found*

**Ketubot 105b** — "כׇּל הַמֵּבִיא דּוֹרוֹן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם — כְּאִילּוּ מַקְרִיב בִּכּוּרִים". Whoever brings a gift to a Torah scholar is as though he offered first-fruits. The Gemara learns it from the "bread of first-fruits" brought to Elisha (II Kings 4:42). *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Mesillat Yesharim 26:12** (Mussar) — Ramchal says that the food a holy man eats is raised up as if offered on the altar, because the Shechinah rests on him as it rested in the Temple. He brings the same two proofs, Ketubot 105b and Yoma 71a.
כֵּן הַמַּאֲכָל וְהַמִּשְׁתֶּה שֶׁהָאִישׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ אוֹכֵל, עִלּוּי הוּא לַמַּאֲכָל הַהוּא וְלַמִּשְׁתֶּה הַהוּא, וּכְאִלּוּ נִקְרָב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מַמָּשׁ

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:72** (Kabbalah) — R. Eliyahu de Vidas explains this Zohar. Scholars do eat ordinary food, but the flow from above inside the food reaches each person by the level of his soul. For the companions it is fine and spiritual, food for the soul. This is close to Rav Tzadok's "מוצא פי ה' שבמאכל".
שֶׁהַמָּזוֹן, יִרְצֶה שֶׁהַשֶּׁפַע הָעֶלְיוֹן, יִהְיֶה נִשְׁפָּע בַּמָּזוֹן הַגַּשְׁמִי הַזֶּה שֶׁאָדָם אוֹכֵל, לְפִי מַדְרֵגַת נִשְׁמַת הָאָדָם

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Miketz 6** (Rav Tzadok) — Yosef's Shabbat meal for his brothers. The Shabbat meal is "סעודתא דמלכא", eaten like sacrifices; he cites Berakhot 10b, Yoma 71a, Zohar II 61b and "מי עדיפת לן מינה". He adds that the extra soul of Shabbat is a Torah scholar hosted in every Jew's home, and that holy eating repairs the first sin, which came through eating. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Yitro 12** (Rav Tzadok) — refers back to this os by name ("ונת' תולדות מא' ג"): holy eating is greater than sacrifices, as Yaakov told Yitzchak, and the Shabbat meal is holy and higher than sacrifices. So at the Shabbat table we ask for His holiness to be revealed, as "הריני נגלה עליו ומברכו" was said of Avraham. *checked*

**Shabbat 119a** — "אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי הֲוָה יָדְעִיתוּן דְּאָתֵינָא? אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִי עֲדִיפַתְּ לַן מִינַּהּ?" Rabbah bar Rav Huna was served a lavish meal and asked whether they had known he was coming. They answered: are you more important to us than she (Shabbat)? The honor due a visiting scholar is what Shabbat gets. So on Shabbat every Jew is like a scholar, and his meal is like eating sacrifices. The story appears again in Chullin 111a. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Sh'lach 11** (Rav Tzadok) — on "נהוריה ישרי בה". He quotes Zohar II 61b on the companions' food and says that on Shabbat all Israel toil in Torah, are "distinguished in halakha" (Berakhot 8a), and so have the scholar's level, with the hint "מי עדיפת לן מינה". He adds Avot 3:3 and "זה השלחן אשר לפני ה'" and the Zohar's reading of the meal's washings and Birkas HaMazon as offerings. *checked*

**Zohar I 142a–b (Toldos)** — "בְּהַהוּא זִמְנָא, עֶרֶב פֶּסַח הֲוָה ... וְעַל דָּא עָבְדַת תְּרֵי תַּבְשִׁילִין. רִבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר, רָמַז הָכָא דְּזַמִּינִין בְּנוֹי דְיַעֲקֹב לְקָרְבָא שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירִים ... וּמִתַּרְוַיְיהוּ טָעִים יִצְחָק וְאָכִיל". It was Erev Pesach, so Rivkah made two dishes. R. Yehudah said this hints at the two Yom Kippur goats, one for Hashem and one to subdue Esav's level, and Yitzchak tasted from both. Rav Tzadok reads the two views as the two kinds of meal: a mitzvah meal, or an actual offering. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Sulam on Zohar, Toldot 129** (Kabbalah) — R. Yehuda Ashlag also reads the passage as a dispute ("וזהו הפלוגתא"). In one view the kids are Pesach and Chagigah, both fully holy. In the other they are the two Yom Kippur goats, one of which normally goes to the other side. Isaac tasted from both because his holiness raised even the left side back to holiness. Rav Tzadok frames the same dispute in terms of holy eating.
אֲבָל עִם כָּל זֶה לֹא הָיָה הֶאָרַת הַשְּׂמֹאל שֶׁבְּכָאן נִשְׁלָח לַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא כְּמוֹ הָעֲזָאזֵל, אֶלָּא וּמִתַּרְוַיְיהוּ טָעִים יִצְחָק

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Ketem Paz on Zohar 142a:3** (Kabbalah) — R. Shimon Lavi takes the Erev Pesach view as Pesach and Chagigah (after Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer). He explains "from both Isaac tasted" by Isaac's attribute reaching even the realm of the shell. He also notes that the Zohar says "tasted" and "ate": the tasting was spiritual and the eating physical.
וְהִסְתַּכֵּל אָמְרוּ טָעִים וְאָכַל כִּי הֵם שְׁנֵי עִנְיָנִים הַטְּעִימָה רוּחָנִית וְהָאֲכִילָה גַּשְׁמִית

**Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 32** (unnamed; quoted in Rashi on Genesis 27:9) — "וְכִי שְׁנֵי גְּדָיֵי עִזִּים הָיָה מַאֲכָלוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק? ... אֶלָּא אֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד הַפֶּסַח וְאֶחָד לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ מַטְעַמִּים". Did Yitzchak really eat two kids? One was for the Pesach, the other for delicacies. Rav Tzadok's "Pesach and Chagigah" follows the later form found in the Shelah and the Bnei Yissaschar: one kid for the Pesach, one for the Chagigah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:20** — "וַיֹּאמֶר יִצְחָק אֶל בְּנוֹ מַה זֶּה מִהַרְתָּ לִמְצֹא בְּנִי וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי הִקְרָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְפָנָי". "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" "Because Hashem your God made it happen before me." *Mafteach: found*

**Bereishit Rabbah 65:19** — "אִם לְקָרְבָּנְךָ הִמְצִיא לְךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיִּשָּׂא אַבְרָהָם אֶת עֵינָיו וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה אַיִל, לְמַאֲכָלְךָ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה". If for your offering the Holy One provided (the ram at the Akeidah), how much more for your food. Rav Tzadok reads the kal vachomer literally: Yitzchak's food ranks above an offering. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Avodat Yisrael, Toldot** (Chassidus) — the Maggid of Kozhnitz reads Yaakov's answer as a hint. Yaakov knew his father ate in holiness and purity and made unions above through his eating. He adds a kal vachomer of his own: if an altar of earth and wood atones, all the more a table eaten in holiness. On "ואברככה לפני ה'" he says that Rivkah understood Yitzchak's hint.
כִּי יָדַע יַעֲקֹב קְדוּשַּׁת אָבִיו שֶׁאוֹכֵל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה וְעוֹשֶׂה יִחוּדִים נִפְלָאִים עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָתוֹ

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 4** (Rav Tzadok) — the next os develops the same kal vachomer. Berakhot 10b says "as though he offers", which suggests the lesser thing; Rav Tzadok answers that both are true. From the side of the host, the offering is greater. Before Hashem, a scholar's eating is dearer than the altar's. He adds that Yitzchak's meal and wine were a taste of the feast of the righteous in the World to Come. *checked*

**Genesis 27:7** (as reported by Rivkah) — "הָבִיאָה לִּי צַיִד וַעֲשֵׂה לִי מַטְעַמִּים וְאֹכֵלָה וַאֲבָרֶכְכָה לִפְנֵי ה' לִפְנֵי מוֹתִי". Yitzchak's own words in 27:4 have no "לפני ה'". Rivkah adds it, and Rav Tzadok takes it as her knowing that his table is "the table before Hashem". *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:4** — "וַעֲשֵׂה לִי מַטְעַמִּים כַּאֲשֶׁר אָהַבְתִּי וְהָבִיאָה לִּי וְאֹכֵלָה בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרֶכְךָ נַפְשִׁי בְּטֶרֶם אָמוּת". Make me delicacies as I love. Out of humility Yitzchak asks only for a mitzvah meal "as I love", that is, as always, without claiming the level of an offering. The second half of the verse is quoted in [1.65]. *Mafteach: missing*

**Megillah 26b** (unnamed) — "תַּשְׁמִישֵׁי מִצְוָה — נִזְרָקִין. תַּשְׁמִישֵׁי קְדוּשָּׁה — נִגְנָזִין". Articles used for a mitzvah (sukkah, lulav, shofar, tzitzis) may be thrown away. Articles of holiness (tefillin, mezuzos, Torah covers) must be stored away. Rav Tzadok maps the two halakhic categories onto the two kinds of meal. *Mafteach: missing*

**Shabbat 22a** — "בַּמֶּה שֶׁשָּׁפַךְ יְכַסֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא יְכַסֶּנּוּ בָּרֶגֶל, שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִצְוֹת בְּזוּיוֹת עָלָיו". One covers the blood with the hand he slaughtered with, not with his foot, so that mitzvos are not treated with contempt. Even a mitzvah article has holiness while the mitzvah is being done. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Agra DeKala, Toldot** (Chassidus) — R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov asks why Yitzchak said "תברכך נפשי" and not "I will bless you". He answers that "my soul" is the Shechinah, the soul of the righteous. Rivkah understood this and said "ואברככה לפני ה'". Rav Tzadok links the same two verses: during the meal the Shechinah rests on Yitzchak and the blessings come from it.
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הַכַּוָּנָה עַל הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהִיא נֶפֶשׁ הַצַּדִּיקִים

**Genesis 27:19** — "קוּם נָא שְׁבָה וְאׇכְלָה מִצֵּידִי בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרְכַנִּי נַפְשֶׁךָ". Yaakov repeats Yitzchak's wording, keeping to the level of a mitzvah meal. With "כי הקרה" in the next verse he hints at the higher level. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:17** — "וַתִּתֵּן אֶת הַמַּטְעַמִּים וְאֶת הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂתָה בְּיַד יַעֲקֹב בְּנָהּ". She put the delicacies and the bread she had made into the hand of Yaakov her son. Rav Tzadok asks why "the bread" is mentioned at all. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Genesis 27:16; correct: Genesis 27:17)*

**Rashi on Leviticus 21:17** — "לֶחֶם אֱלֹהָיו. מַאֲכַל אֱלֹהָיו, כָּל סְעוּדָה קְרוּיָה לֶחֶם, כְּמוֹ 'עֲבַד לְחֶם רַב'". "Bread of his God" means His food, because every meal is called bread, as in "he made a great feast". Rav Tzadok shows that this does not explain the doubled wording here. The Mafteach indexes only the Daniel verse. *Mafteach: missing*
**Daniel 5:1** — "בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר מַלְכָּא עֲבַד לְחֶם רַב לְרַבְרְבָנוֹהִי אֲלַף". King Belshazzar made a great feast (lechem) for a thousand of his lords. *Mafteach: found*

**Leviticus 21:6** — "כִּי אֶת אִשֵּׁי ה' לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיהֶם הֵם מַקְרִיבִם". The priests offer Hashem's fire-offerings, the bread of their God. Offerings are called "bread", so "the bread" Rivkah gave marks the meal as an offering. *Mafteach: missing*

**Numbers 28:2** — "אֶת קׇרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי רֵיחַ נִיחֹחִי תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ". My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings. Rav Tzadok uses it again in [2.26]. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי
notes.text: **Exodus 20:21** (20:24 in some numberings) — "מִזְבַּח אֲדָמָה תַּעֲשֶׂה לִּי ... בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ". In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned I will come to you and bless you. The verse is said of the altar. Yitzchak's blessings after the meal are the altar's "וברכתיך". *Mafteach: found*

**Bereishit Rabbah 48:5** (opening of Vayera) — "מָה אִם זֶה שֶׁהִקְרִיב שׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁמִי הֲרֵינִי נִגְלָה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ, אַבְרָהָם שֶׁמָּל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁמִי עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה". This is R. Levi's opening. The preceding opening (48:4, R. Yitzchak) makes the same point from "מזבח אדמה" with "שבנה מזבח". Rav Tzadok quotes R. Levi's wording. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayera 7** (Rav Tzadok) — asks where any blessing appears in Avraham's revelation. He answers that Hashem's blessing is growth in the Oral Torah (Sefer HaBahir: Torah is called blessing). So "I will come to you and bless you" is the light of the Oral Torah. This matches [2.23]–[2.27]: "My Name" and "His bread" are words of Torah. *checked*

**Berakhot 6a** — "וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמּוֹ — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ". The Gemara moves the altar verse to Torah study: even one person learning alone has the Shechinah with him. *Mafteach: found*

**Menachot 110a** on **Leviticus 7:37** — "אָמַר רָבָא: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לֹא עוֹלָה וְלֹא מִנְחָה וְלֹא חַטָּאת וְלֹא אָשָׁם". Rava: one who studies Torah needs no burnt-offering, meal-offering, sin-offering or guilt-offering. Resh Lakish had said only "as though he offered"; Rava's reading makes Torah greater than the offerings. The Mafteach has the daf but not the verse. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 8a** — "מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה בִּלְבַד". Since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One has in His world only the four cubits of halakha. The place of halakha takes over the altar's holiness. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 21a** on **Deuteronomy 32:3** — "מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי שֵׁם ה' אֶקְרָא, הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ". The blessing before Torah study comes from "When I call the Name of Hashem". So "Name" means words of Torah, and "where I cause My Name to be mentioned" is Torah spoken at the meal. *Mafteach: found*

**Tamid 32b** — "כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה בַּלַּיְלָה — שְׁכִינָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ". Whoever studies Torah at night, the Shechinah faces him. Rav Tzadok's wording, "the Holy One sits and studies opposite him", is closest to **Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 18**: "כָּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְקוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה ... הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב כְּנֶגְדּוֹ וְקוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה עִמּוֹ". It shows the "awakening Above" in answer to Torah below. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:25** — "וַיַּגֶּשׁ לוֹ וַיֹּאכַל וַיָּבֵא לוֹ יַיִן וַיֵּשְׁתְּ". Yitzchak had asked only for delicacies, yet Yaakov also brought wine. Each of the two views gives the wine a meaning: the four cups of Pesach, or the libations. *Mafteach: missing*

**Mishnah Pesachim 10:1** (unnamed) — "וְלֹא יִפְחֲתוּ לוֹ מֵאַרְבַּע כּוֹסוֹת שֶׁל יַיִן, וַאֲפִלּוּ מִן הַתַּמְחוּי". On Pesach night no one may have fewer than four cups of wine, even a poor man fed from the charity plate. *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereishit Rabbah 65:14** — "טוֹבִים, רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר: טוֹבִים לְךָ, שֶׁעַל יָדָן אַתְּ נוֹטֵל אֶת הַבְּרָכוֹת. וְטוֹבִים לְבָנֶיךָ, שֶׁעַל יָדָן הוּא מִתְכַּפֵּר לָהֶם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים". The kids are good for you, since through them you take the blessings, and good for your children, since through them they are atoned on Yom Kippur. This is the Midrash's hint at the Yom Kippur view. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereishit Rabbah 65:15** on **Leviticus 16:22** — "וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר עָלָיו, זֶה עֵשָׂו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הֵן עֵשָׂו אָחִי אִישׁ שָׂעִר. אֶת כׇּל עֲוֹנֹתָם, עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם". "The goat shall carry on itself" is Esav, the hairy man. "Their sins" (עונתם) are the sins of the tam, Yaakov. *Mafteach: found*

**Eruvin 13b** — "יָצְאָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים הֵן, וַהֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל". After three years of dispute between Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel, a heavenly voice declared that both are the words of the living God. Here Rav Tzadok applies it to the Zohar's two views of Rivkah's two kids. *Mafteach: found*

**Kedushat Levi, Leviticus, Homily for Pesach 17** — "אֲבָל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵד אֶת הַבּוֹרֵא בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּמְעוֹרֵר הַמִּדּוֹת ... וְכֵן הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת שְׁנֵי יוֹם טוֹב בְּיוֹם אֶחָד". The Berditchever answers the paytan who says in one place that Avraham was circumcised on Pesach and in another on Yom Kippur. Avraham, the lone servant who aroused the attributes, could make any day a festival by the attribute he aroused: love made it Pesach, fear made it Yom Kippur. Rav Tzadok quotes the passage almost word for word. *Mafteach: missing*

**Berakhot 49a** (the idea behind Kedushat Levi's phrase) — "מְקַדֵּשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזְּמַנִּים — יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּקַדְּשִׁינְהוּ לִזְמַנִּים". The festival blessing names Israel before the seasons, because Israel sanctifies the seasons. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ezekiel 33:24** — "אֶחָד הָיָה אַבְרָהָם וַיִּירַשׁ אֶת הָאָרֶץ". Avraham was one, and he inherited the land. Kedushat Levi uses the verse for Avraham as the lone individual who aroused the divine attributes. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 120:2** with **Zohar I 143a (Toldos)** — "ה' הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה, דָּא הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְעֵשָׂו שַׁרְיָא בֵּיהּ, דְּאִיהוּ שְׂפַת שֶׁקֶר". Hashem, save my soul from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue; this is the level Esav dwells in, the lip of falsehood. The Zohar puts this prayer in Yaakov's mouth as he goes in to his father. For Rav Tzadok, Yaakov's anguish here draws down the forgiveness of Yom Kippur. *Mafteach: found*

**Mishnah Yoma 6:1** (Bavli Yoma 62a) — "שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, מִצְוָתָן שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שָׁוִין בְּמַרְאֶה וּבְקוֹמָה וּבְדָמִים וּבִלְקִיחָתָן כְּאֶחָד". The two Yom Kippur goats should be alike in look, height and price, and bought together. So the goat "for Azazel" is also a consecrated offering, like Rivkah's second kid. *Mafteach: found*
